title: Share tree type data across a forest
description: A forest can contain thousands of trees. Each tree has a unique position (x, y) but shares species, color, and texture with all trees of the same type. TreeType holds the shared data. TreeFactory caches TreeType instances so each combination is only created once. Forest plants trees by going through the factory — never creating TreeType directly. Implement TreeFactory and Forest.
hints: TreeFactory should cache by a key that combines species, color, and texture — not species alone
Forest holds a TreeFactory internally; plantTree() calls getTreeType() to get the shared instance
The proof that Flyweight is working: 1000 oak trees share exactly one TreeType instance
issues: Without sharing, every tree stores its own copy of species, color, and texture
A forest of 10 000 oak trees would create 10 000 identical TreeType objects
overallGoal: Use the Flyweight pattern so Forest can plant thousands of trees while only creating one TreeType per unique species+color+texture combination, with reference equality as proof of sharing.
goals: TreeFactory.getTreeType() returns the same instance for the same species+color+texture combination
Forest.plantTree() uses the factory to obtain a shared TreeType before creating each Tree
A forest of many same-species trees has far fewer TreeType instances than Tree instances
